claims.text: Single-phase ZrB2 normally requires sintering above 2300 °C to achieve high densification and structural integrity.
Approximately 3 wt% elemental Si should be added to ZrB2 powder.
Si-doped ZrB2 can be densified by rapid sintering, such as spark plasma sintering, at about 1700 °C.
A short hold of about 10 minutes in an inert atmosphere at about 1700 °C will promote liquid-phase sintering.
Silicon forms a transient liquid phase during sintering.
The transient Si-containing liquid enhances particle rearrangement and densification.
Silicon segregates into Si-rich intergranular or grain-boundary regions.
Grain-boundary silicon converts into a silica-like phase during oxidation.
The Si-derived silica phase limits oxygen ingress.
The Si-derived intergranular phase limits penetration by liquid plating metals or other corrosive species.
Reduced porosity from Si-assisted densification improves particle bonding and mechanical integrity.

Si-doped ZrB2 sintered at about 1700 °C will exhibit improved densification and mechanical strength relative to conventional high-temperature single-phase ZrB2 and lower-temperature undoped specimens.
Si-doped ZrB2 will show less oxidation-related weight gain at 1200 °C than both comparison materials.
Si-doped ZrB2 will have a lower liquid-metal corrosion rate in simulated plating-bath conditions than both comparison materials.
Lower-temperature ZrB2 specimens made without silicon generally have incomplete densification, poor oxidation resistance, or vulnerability to liquid-metal corrosion.
The proposed intervention is applicable near 3 wt% Si and a sintering temperature near 1700 °C.
The proposed protection is expected to remain effective in air up to about 1200 °C.
The proposed protection is expected to remain effective in molten tin or similar alloy plating baths at relevant service temperatures.
